x: ModifyDBInstance applies a fixed subset of fields (class, storage, engine version, backup retention, master password); other settings are stored and returned but not individually validated.

features.t: SQL execution (Query editor / RDS Data API)
x: The data plane is a real engine (sqlite3 by default, PGlite real Postgres on Nano) reached only through the RDS Data API (ExecuteStatement/BatchExecuteStatement) — Vyomi does not expose the Postgres/MySQL wire protocol directly, so an unmodified psycopg2/mysqlclient TCP connection cannot reach it.
Subnet IDs and the VPC are stored and returned exactly as given; Vyomi does not validate that they exist in a real VPC (it does not model EC2/VPC in depth for RDS).

Parameters are stored and returned exactly as modified (ModifyDBParameterGroup round-trips through DescribeDBParameters). max_connections is ENFORCED against the RDS Data API's real transactions (rds.data-api) — BeginTransaction on an instance already at its parameter group's max_connections is rejected, not silently accepted; lowering/raising the value genuinely changes that ceiling. Every other parameter (shared_buffers, log_min_duration_statement, innodb_buffer_pool_size, …) remains stored/returned only, with no effect on the underlying SQL engine.
Vyomi logs its own control-plane actions (create/modify/delete/lifecycle/snapshot); it does not generate the full category list AWS produces (e.g. failover, low-storage).
Creating, listing and deleting a DB proxy record is real and stateful; Vyomi does not actually proxy connections through it — apps still connect straight to the instance's own endpoint.
Option group metadata CRUD is real; adding/removing individual options within a group is not modeled — Vyomi has no engine-specific option catalogue (e.g. Oracle APEX, SQL Server TDE).

An enabled subscription whose SourceType/EventCategories match really publishes to its SnsTopicArn (through the same sns_core.publish_arn seam EventBridge targets use) when the matching RDS control-plane event fires — not just a stored record. Delivery covers the same control-plane events rds.events logs (create/modify/delete/lifecycle/snapshot); AWS's fuller category list (e.g. failover, low-storage) isn't generated, matching rds.events' own scope.

The current-region automated backup window is derived from the live instance's retention setting (DescribeDBInstanceAutomatedBackups); cross-region replication of backups and backups retained after instance deletion are not modeled.

features.t: CloudWatch metrics on the DB instance detail page
x: DatabaseConnections (the instance's real count of currently open RDS Data API transactions) and ReadIOPS/WriteIOPS (a real count of SELECT vs. write statements actually executed through the RDS Data API / query editor) are genuine datapoints pushed to CloudWatch (AWS/RDS namespace) as the activity happens — GetMetricStatistics/GetMetricData return real series, not synthetic ones.

Vyomi derives one real error-log file per DB instance (error/postgresql.log or error/mysql-error-running.log, via the native DescribeDBLogFiles/DownloadDBLogFilePortion actions) from genuine SQL execution failures raised through the RDS Data API / query editor — an instance with no failed statements has an empty log, not a fabricated one.

features.t: Read replicas, Multi-AZ failover, connected compute resources, security group rules
x: CreateDBInstanceReadReplica/PromoteReadReplica are real, stateful: a replica is a genuine, independent DB instance, linked bidirectionally to its source, that cannot be deleted while replicas exist. Every autocommit write (ExecuteStatement without a transactionId) on the source is really replayed against each replica's own engine as it happens, so a replica's data genuinely reflects the source's writes — statements run inside an explicit BeginTransaction are NOT forwarded (replicas are independent engines, not a shared WAL), so lag is effectively zero for the path that is replicated and undefined for the path that isn't.

PurchaseReservedDBInstancesOffering records a real, stateful reservation (DescribeReservedDBInstances lists it); Vyomi has no billing system and no reserved-instance-offering catalogue, so the console's purchase wizard (pricing, terms, offering ids) is not built — call the action directly with a reservation id.

There is no public RDS capacity-reservation API and Vyomi has no billing or capacity market: a reservation is a record (Vyomi-only service vyomi-reservations: DB instance class, instance count 1-100, optional Availability Zone / engine / end date) and nothing is actually held back from other workloads. Utilization is real: the available DB instances of the same class (and AZ / engine when given) are counted against the reserved count - used, unused and over-subscribed instances are reported.

The integration really replicates: DynamoDB table items / RDS table rows are copied into an in-process 'Redshift-lite' warehouse (sqlite) on every touch/query ('sync on read'), and the Redshift Data API (ExecuteStatement/GetStatementResult, CREATE DATABASE ... FROM INTEGRATION) queries it. The SQL dialect is SQLite's, not Redshift's; replication is poll-on-touch, not a continuous stream; no data filters, encryption or cross-account semantics; the warehouse is in memory and rebuilt from the sources on boot. A real Redshift/SageMaker lakehouse is not run.

CreateCustomDBEngineVersion/DeleteCustomDBEngineVersion/DescribeDBEngineVersions registers real, stateful install-media metadata; RDS Custom itself (the customer-managed EC2 instance the engine actually runs on) is out of Vyomi's scope entirely — the console's create wizard is not built.

DescribeDBRecommendations derives four real advisories from each instance's own live configuration (no Multi-AZ, an outdated CA certificate, automated backups disabled, deletion protection disabled); Vyomi has no general analysis engine, so it does not generate the full category of recommendations AWS's own monitoring produces (e.g. storage autoscaling, parameter tuning).

StartExportTask writes the snapshot's real table data as gzip-compressed Apache Parquet into the simulator's OWN S3 store (never AWS) in AWS's layout — <prefix>/<task>/<database>/<schema>.<table>/part-00000-<id>.gz.parquet plus export_info_<task>.json and export_tables_info_<task>_from_1_to_<N>.json. Offline the Parquet writer is pyarrow; in Nano it is the vendored parquet-wasm 0.7.1 + apache-arrow 18.1.0 (lazy-loaded on the first export). If the Parquet engine is unavailable or fails, or the bucket doesn't exist, the task FAILS with a FailureCause — there is no fallback format.

CACertificateIdentifier is validated on CreateDBInstance/ModifyDBInstance against a real, small CA catalog (DescribeCertificates) — the same identifiers and validity windows AWS publishes (rds-ca-rsa2048-g1, rds-ca-rsa4096-g1, rds-ca-ecc384-g1, the retired rds-ca-2019); an unknown id is rejected (CertificateNotFound), and any instance whose CA differs from the current default is flagged on the certificate-update page with its REAL ValidFrom/ValidTill (no more placeholder dates), with a working 'Apply update now' that really calls ModifyDBInstance. Vyomi does not enforce wall-clock cert expiry at connection time — a cert past its ValidTill doesn't actually block anything.

features.t: IAM role association for RDS features (AddRoleToDBInstance / RemoveRoleFromDBInstance / AssociatedRoles)
x: The role must exist in Vyomi's IAM and trust rds.amazonaws.com, and the feature must be one the engine supports (checked against AWS's per-engine list); associations are stored and returned like the real API. The database engines in Vyomi do not actually assume the role, so s3Import/s3Export through the role is not performed — S3 exports use Vyomi's own export-task path (rds.exports-to-s3).

features.t: CloudWatch alarms for a DB instance (create, list, delete, SNS action) in the Logs & events tab
x: Real CloudWatch alarms on AWS/RDS metrics with the DBInstanceIdentifier dimension. Only DatabaseConnections, ReadIOPS and WriteIOPS carry data (see rds.monitoring); alarms on CPUUtilization, FreeStorageSpace or FreeableMemory exist but stay INSUFFICIENT_DATA because Vyomi has no virtualized compute/disk to measure.

features.t: Dashboard and Service quotas pages (DescribeAccountAttributes: default quotas + live usage)
x: Quota maxima are AWS's default RDS quotas for us-east-1 and cannot be raised (no Service Quotas increase workflow). Usage is counted from the live store (instances, allocated storage, subnet groups, snapshots, roles, proxies); the dashboard's DB clusters count is 0 because Aurora clusters aren't modeled.

RestoreDBInstanceFromS3 validates like the real API (MySQL only, required parameters, role ARN, existing identifier, missing bucket or empty prefix -> InvalidS3BucketFault) and builds a new instance from backup files in the simulator's own S3. Real RDS reads a Percona XtraBackup physical backup, which cannot be replayed here: Vyomi reads .sql / .sql.gz logical dumps (mysqldump output is normalised for the engine: LOCK/UNLOCK/SET/USE statements, ENGINE=/CHARSET=/AUTO_INCREMENT= options and inline KEY lines are dropped) and, on the offline appliance only, the Parquet files of an RDS snapshot export. Auto-increment behaviour, stored routines, triggers, views and users in a dump are not preserved by the instance's engine, a failing statement leaves the instance in incompatible-restore, and an XtraBackup file is refused.

features.t: Data migrations (AWS DMS between simulator databases)
x: Real DMS control plane (core/dms_core.py, target AmazonDMSv20160101): replication instances, source/target endpoints, TestConnection, replication tasks with selection-rule TableMappings, DescribeTableStatistics. An endpoint's ServerName must resolve to a simulator RDS instance; StartReplicationTask really creates the selected tables on the target instance and copies the rows.

features.t: Database Insights (DB load, cache hit ratio, commits/rollbacks, deadlocks)
x: DBLoad (average active sessions from pg_stat_activity), BufferCacheHitRatio, TransactionCommits/Rollbacks and Deadlocks are read from pg_stat_database / pg_stat_activity by the collector (offline Postgres every 30 s, or pushed to /_obs/rds-stats) and published to CloudWatch AWS/RDS. pg_stat_database is database-wide, so instances sharing one Postgres (schema-per-instance) share these counters. Engines that cannot answer pg_stat (in-memory sqlite) publish nothing. No Top SQL / wait events. Nano PGlite uses the async collector (acollect_rds_stats) but no timer drives it yet.
